findings.message: This fix compares owner names in two ways that can disagree. `same` uses a trimmed, case-sensitive match against the stored owner_name. `ownerLink` (common.ts) uses a trimmed, case-insensitive match against the actor's name. If someone restates the current owner in a different case, `same` is false, so the update goes through `ownerLink`. Unless the actor is that owner, `ownerLink` returns null, which clears a valid user link and records the owner as unlinked. The test only covers an exact restatement. Fix: use one name-normalising helper for both comparisons, for example trim plus a locale-insensitive lower-case. Add case and spacing variants to the table-driven test.
findings.scenario: PS-0142 is owned by 'Nimal Silva' and linked to Nimal's user. Liam confirms update_opportunity { ownerName: 'nimal silva' } → `same` is false and ownerLink(Liam, 'nimal silva') returns null → owner_user_id is set to null and the result says ownerLinked: false, though the owner did not change.

findings.message: The page now follows a re-tagged release to its new URL, but the fix stops at the URL. The comment says `router.replace` keeps the conversation open on the new page. That conversation still holds the old pins: the release pin and the new `deployPin`, both `{ projectKey, version: 'v2.4.0' }` (ReleasePage.tsx:16-18). On the next turn those pins resolve to a release that no longer exists. Pins saved in `chat.conversation` have the same problem. The new `get_deployment` makes it worse: it keys a deployment by its immutable uuid but still requires the mutable version. Fix: when `moved` is applied, rewrite the pins in this conversation whose args name the old version. Also make `get_deployment` resolve by `deploymentId` alone, with project and version only as a scope check.
findings.scenario: On /delivery/releases/CON/v2.4.0, pin the Prod deployment row. Ask amax to re-tag to v2.4.1 and confirm. The page moves to v2.4.1. Then type 'void this deployment, wrong pipeline'. The pinned get_deployment {version:'v2.4.0', deploymentId} returns null, so chat reports the record as not found.

findings.message: The person only learns that the owner link will be cleared (`ownerLinked: false` and the note) after confirming. The confirm card they approve does not mention it. Show this on the pending action, or reject an unlinkable owner name until the person confirms they want a name-only owner.
findings.scenario: Liam confirms update_opportunity { ownerName: 'Ama Perera (fictional)' } on an opportunity linked to a user → the link is cleared, and the warning appears only in the result after the write.

findings.message: weekIds only accepts names without ',' or '('. Any other display name, such as 'Silva, Nimal' or a fixture name with '(fictional)', makes the whole bulk prompt map to zero calls. The scripted model then silently does nothing instead of failing the e2e step. Match from the '(week id <uuid>)' anchors instead, or throw when the list doesn't parse.
findings.scenario: Approve the submitted timesheets for 2026-W42: Ama Perera (fictional) (week id <uuid>) → weekIds returns [] → no approve_week call is made.

findings.message: The name is trimmed, but the employee-number match is not. A padded employee number misses the exact match, falls through to the name match and returns null ('not found'). Trim `ref.person` once and use it for both matches.
findings.scenario: get_allocation { person: ' LL-0002' } → null, though LL-0002 is visible in the grid.

findings.message: getProposal and getEnvironment match the key and name exactly, so case matters. Chat or MCP callers can pass free text, which then reads as 'not found'. Fix: normalise the lookup, the same way the other key lookups in this module are done.
findings.scenario: get_proposal {key:'con-017'} returns null, although CON-017 exists.
